children: The eurozone's adjusted trade surplus widened in July, signaling a boost to the economy from trade at the start of the third quarter despite lingering geopolitical uncertainty.

The trade in goods surplus of the 21-nation currency area was 5.0 billion euros in the month ($5.77 billion), compared with a surplus of 1.0 billion euros in June, statistics agency Eurostat said Tuesday.
Adjusted exports rose 1.2%, while imports declined 0.4%, it said.

"The increase was mainly driven by a higher surplus in chemicals and related products, in other manufactured goods and food and drink," Eurostat said. This was partially offset by a fall in the surplus for machinery and vehicles, it added.

title: Eurozone Trade Surplus Widened in July
